title: Unpermitted Kitchen Island Blueprint Dispute
brief: Explain to a homeowner why their custom kitchen island layout violates safety codes and negotiate a compliant solution.

edge.scenario: You are on site at a residential remodel in suburban Ohio preparing to pull wire for a new kitchen island. The homeowner has handed you an unpermitted Pinterest-inspired layout that places high-voltage outlets directly below an undermount sink and omits required dedicated circuits. Drywall starts tomorrow morning, and she is demanding you wire it exactly according to her sketch.
edge.personaPublic: Diane is a stressed homeowner overseeing her own kitchen remodel, juggling sub-contractors on a tight budget. She looks anxious and defensive, holding her printout firmly while gesturing around the framed kitchen.
edge.personaHidden: She poured her remaining savings into custom quartz countertops that are being cut off-site this afternoon based strictly on this sketch. She is terrified that moving any wiring or outlets will force an expensive recut of the stone that she cannot afford.
edge.goal: Explain the National Electrical Code safety hazards clearly and agree on an alternative outlet placement that satisfies code without compromising her custom countertop fabrication.

criteria.text: Acknowledges her design vision and tight timeline before citing regulations
Explains the fire and shock hazard plainly without using dense code jargon
Identifies the core constraint driving her reluctance to alter the plan
Offers compliant alternative placements such as pop-up outlets or side-panel mounts
Agrees on an updated sketch mark-up to finalize before rough-in begins

edge.opening: Look, I know what the standard blueprint says, but I specifically designed this island layout myself. I need these outlets right here under the sink edge, and the drywall crew arrives at seven tomorrow morning. Can you just hook it up to the existing line so we don't fall behind?
